meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The best revenge is massive success'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Frank Sinatra with no source, and separately to Les Brown. A free-floating motivational line, not a documented Sinatra quote.

answer.label: Not verified as Frank Sinatra — an unsourced modern maxim
answer.sourceLine: This line is credited to Sinatra on thousands of quote pages, but no interview, recording, memoir, or biography is ever cited, and it does not appear in Wikiquote’s Sinatra entry at all. The same words are separately attributed to motivational speaker Les Brown — the signature of a free-floating success maxim rather than a documented quotation. Its ancestral idea is the 1640 proverb “Living well is the best revenge.”

source.excerpt: The best revenge is massive success.
trail: Quote Investigator traces the older saying “Living well is the best revenge” to George Herbert’s Outlandish Proverbs (1640), but does not document any Sinatra “massive success” variant.
Wikiquote’s Sinatra page does not list this line at all — not in the sourced section, not even among misattributions.
Sean Croxton’s Quote of the Day presents the identical wording as something “Les Brown says,” showing the line floats between famous names.
Quote-aggregator pages such as Quoteikon print it as a Sinatra quote while supplying no citation, date, or occasion.
source.excerptNote: Reproduced as it circulates; no primary source attaches it to Sinatra.

source.rightsNote: Because the exact wording cannot be tied to any dated, identifiable first publication — it circulates anonymously and is credited to several people — no copyright status can be responsibly asserted. The ancestral proverb “Living well is the best revenge” (George Herbert, 1640) is public domain, but that is a different sentence.

author.name: Frank Sinatra
author.heading: About Frank Sinatra
author.metaLine: 1915–1998 · American singer & actor, the archetypal comeback star
author.bio: Frank Sinatra was one of the best-selling recording artists of the 20th century and an Academy Award–winning actor whose career arced through spectacular slumps and even more spectacular comebacks. That biography — counted out, then roaring back bigger — is exactly why a triumph-over-critics line sticks to his name so readily. But a quote fitting a person’s story is not the same as evidence they said it.

The “massive success” wording circulates unsourced under Frank Sinatra’s name and, separately, Les Brown’s.

misattribution.heading: How a slogan got pinned on Sinatra
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook feel-good attribution: a punchy success maxim with no traceable source, attached to a famous name whose life story makes it feel authentic.

items.why: Repeated on countless quote sites and social posts, yet not one cites an interview, lyric, book, or documented occasion, and it is absent from Wikiquote’s Sinatra entry. Aggregators like Goodreads host it with the standard disclaimer that community quotes are unverified.

Motivational speaker Les Brown delivers the identical line, presented as his own on Sean Croxton’s Quote of the Day — a hallmark of a phrase that belongs to the self-help circuit rather than to one named author.

misattribution.truthLine: The genuine, documented ancestor is a 17th-century proverb — “Living well is the best revenge,” traced by Quote Investigator to George Herbert’s Outlandish Proverbs (1640). The “massive success” rewrite is a modern motivational reworking with no verified author.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Sinatra
lead: Sinatra was the century’s great comeback act — written off, then triumphant, again and again. A line about answering critics with success maps so neatly onto that arc that people assume he must have said it. That fit is precisely what lets an unsourced slogan travel under his name.

The phrase “massive success” itself is a tell: it is the vocabulary of late-20th-century motivational speaking, not of Sinatra’s own recorded remarks. The sentiment is old; this particular packaging is modern.
context.pull: A quote that fits a life is not the same as a quote from that life.
